tool.name: ComputeDerivative
tool.summary: Derivative of a potential-field grid in x, y or z (vertical), to a chosen power. Highlights near-surface, short-wavelength features.
tool.usage: Best applied to a magnetic grid that has been reduced to the pole (RTP) or the equator (RTE).

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: order
param.dialogReference: Power of the derivative: 1 for the first derivative, 2 for the second; fractional powers are allowed.
param.pythonReference: Power of the derivative: 1 for the first derivative, 2 for the second; fractional powers are allowed.

param.name: buffer_size
param.dialogReference: FFT buffer in pixels added around the grid before the Fourier transform, to reduce edge effects. 0 (the default) chooses it as in QGIS: the shorter side of the grid, up to 5000. A value greater than 0 is used as that upper limit instead.
param.pythonReference: FFT buffer in pixels added around the grid before the Fourier transform, to reduce edge effects. 0 (the default) chooses it as in QGIS: the shorter side of the grid, up to 5000. A value greater than 0 is used as that upper limit instead.
